title: High-Throughput Multi-Channel Notification Orchestration Service with Deduplication, Rate Limiting & Channel Fallback
problem: Modern applications communicating across email, SMS, mobile push, and chat channels suffer from duplicate message dispatches, uncoordinated user notification fatigue, and complete delivery failure when third-party gateway providers encounter outages. Tight coupling between business logic and downstream provider APIs creates brittle architectures without centralized delivery tracking or retry backoff. This project builds a high-throughput notification orchestration service in Node.js and TypeScript. The system buffers incoming events using RabbitMQ message queues, deduplicates messages using Redis sliding-window hashes, resolves user channel preferences, enforces per-user rate limits, routes to mock delivery providers with automatic fallback, and maintains an immutable delivery audit log in PostgreSQL.

use_cases.title: E-Commerce Transactional Order & Delivery Notifications
use_cases.first_sentence: Consumer retail platforms need to dispatch order confirmations, shipping updates, and one-time authentication codes reliably across multiple communication channels.
use_cases.second_sentence: The service deduplicates rapid checkout triggers, routes critical delivery updates to mobile push notifications, and automatically falls back to SMS if push tokens are invalid.

use_cases.title: Digital Banking Security & Fraud Alert Dispatch
use_cases.first_sentence: Financial services platforms require immediate, guaranteed delivery of suspicious debit alerts and transaction verification prompts to customer devices.
use_cases.second_sentence: The platform prioritizes critical security alerts through high-priority message queues, tracking delivery confirmations and recording immutable timestamps for compliance audits.

use_cases.title: Enterprise Collaboration Team Notification Digests
use_cases.first_sentence: Project management platforms serving thousands of corporate users need to prevent notification fatigue caused by rapid successive comment notifications.
use_cases.second_sentence: The engine enforces per-user rate limiting and temporal batching, aggregating conversational mentions into formatted email and in-app digest summaries.

hard_parts: Guaranteeing exactly-once notification delivery semantics across distributed workers using atomic Redis deduplication hashes
Designing resilient priority queue topologies in RabbitMQ that prevent high-volume marketing batches from delaying critical authentication alerts
Implementing dynamic channel fallback logic that detects third-party provider timeouts and re-routes messages without losing delivery context
Managing per-user sliding-window rate limiters that prevent alert spam while preserving critical security notification overrides
screener_signals: Clean TypeScript codebase cleanly separating queue consumers, channel provider adapters, user preference resolvers, and audit repositories
High-throughput load benchmark report verifying 2,500+ notifications per second sustained processing with sub-350ms channel fallback
Anti-fake verification script issuing duplicate notification payloads concurrently and verifying exactly one message is dispatched while the duplicate is suppressed

components.name: Notification Ingestion API & Priority RabbitMQ Producer
components.purpose: Ingests notification requests, assigns priority classes, and publishes messages to RabbitMQ topic exchanges

components.name: Redis Event Deduplicator & Rate Limit Guard
components.purpose: Checks SHA-256 event fingerprints to eliminate duplicate dispatches and enforces per-user rate limits

components.name: User Channel Preference & Routing Resolver
components.purpose: Queries recipient preferences, quiet hours, and channel opt-outs to determine the optimal delivery channel

components.name: Multi-Channel Provider Dispatcher & Fallback Engine
components.purpose: Dispatches payloads to mock email, SMS, and push providers, automatically failing over to secondary channels

components.name: Delivery Audit Logger & Benchmark Harness
components.purpose: Records delivery status transitions (Queued, Sent, Delivered, Failed) and benchmarks ingestion throughput

architecture.data_flow: An upstream service dispatches a notification request over REST; the ingestion API computes a SHA-256 event fingerprint; Redis checks whether the fingerprint was processed within the sliding window; if unique, the message publishes to RabbitMQ with a priority header; queue workers consume the message, check user channel preferences and rate limits in PostgreSQL; the worker dispatches the notification to the primary channel adapter (e.g. Push); if the provider times out or fails, the fallback engine re-routes the message to the secondary channel (e.g. SMS); delivery status updates commit to PostgreSQL.
architecture.enforcement_mechanism: Redis SETNX with TTL for atomic idempotency; RabbitMQ dead-letter exchanges (DLX) isolating poisoned messages after 3 retries.

targets.method: Percentage of intentionally duplicated notification payloads correctly suppressed within sliding time window
targets.input: 1,000 paired duplicate notification requests issued simultaneously across 10 concurrent worker threads
targets.environment: Standard 4-core local CPU, Redis 7 in Docker, Node.js 18+ runtime
targets.minimum_pass: 1,000 of 1,000 duplicate payloads suppressed with 0 duplicate delivery executions
targets.target: 1,000 of 1,000 duplicate payloads suppressed with 0 duplicate delivery executions
targets.report: Deduplication benchmark audit log and Redis idempotency verification summary

targets.metric: Sustained Message Ingestion and Routing Throughput
targets.method: Sustained notification requests ingested, deduplicated, and queued per second across RabbitMQ topic exchange
targets.input: 20,000 synthetic notification events published across high and normal priority topics
targets.environment: Standard 4-core local CPU, RabbitMQ 3.12+ in Docker, local network loopback
targets.minimum_pass: Publish throughput is >= 2,500 notifications per second
targets.target: Publish throughput is >= 5,500 notifications per second
targets.report: RabbitMQ ingestion throughput log and performance summary table

targets.method: Duration from primary channel provider timeout detection to successful delivery dispatch via secondary channel
targets.input: 30 simulated primary channel provider failure chaos scenarios during active message processing
targets.environment: Mock provider simulator with configurable latency and error injection (HTTP 500 / timeout)
targets.minimum_pass: Average channel fallback duration is < 350 milliseconds across 30 trials
targets.target: Average channel fallback duration is < 120 milliseconds across 30 trials
targets.report: Provider failover timing report and delivery audit verification

environment.gpu: None required (purely CPU and network I/O bound backend service)

riskiest_component.name: RabbitMQ Memory Pressure and Connection Starvation Under Sudden Event Bursts
riskiest_component.mitigation: Configure prefetch counts on consumer channels, apply message TTLs, and configure RabbitMQ high watermark alarms.
riskiest_component.fallback: Spill excess messages to durable disk-backed dead-letter queues.

worksheet.q1: Core deliverable: a multi-channel notification orchestration service in Node.js/TypeScript with RabbitMQ queues, Redis deduplication, and PostgreSQL audit logging.
worksheet.q2: Target users: backend infrastructure engineers, distributed systems developers, and core platform architects.
worksheet.q3: 3 use cases: e-commerce order status updates, digital banking security alerts, and enterprise team digests.
worksheet.q4: Stated hours: 28 hours. Calculated bottom-up: 24 component hours * 1.15 buffer = 27.6 -> 28 hours. Intermediate level.
worksheet.q5: Hard parts: atomic Redis deduplication hashes, priority queue isolation in RabbitMQ, dynamic channel fallback routing, and sliding-window rate limiting.
worksheet.q6: Starter input: notification event schemas, mock provider simulator scripts, and PostgreSQL migrations. Synthetic mock data only.
